title: The ninth Guru and his three companions
hookLine: Mati Das, Sati Das and Dayala are remembered with Guru Tegh Bahadur each year

lines: STRENGTH IS GONE. BOUND IN CHAINS.
cards: Strength is gone. I'm bound in chains. Nothing I do can help.

That's the sense of a short salok of Guru Tegh Bahadur near the end of the Guru Granth Sahib, and tradition links it to his imprisonment, before his death in Delhi. But he wasn't alone in that prison.
Three men had come with him, and they were put to death before him, tradition says, to break him. Each year, when Sikhs remember the ninth Guru, those three names are said beside his.

teach.h: THREE NAMES, NONE OF THEM GURUS.
teach.b: Bhai Mati Das. His brother, Bhai Sati Das. And Bhai Dayala.

This path met them in the story of Delhi: two brothers and a third companion, all close to the Guru. None of them was a Guru. Tradition says each was offered his life if he gave up his faith, and each refused.

When Sikhs mark Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom, in gurdwaras and at Gurdwara Sis Ganj in Delhi, the three companions are remembered on the same day, beside him. The day belongs to a Guru and his friends.
In the salok from today's opening, on Ang 1429, the ninth Guru says strength is gone and the chains are on, and then turns: now only the Lord is my support.
The very next salok answers it: strength has come, the chains are broken, everything is possible, everything is in your hands.
Tradition holds that this answer came from his son, Guru Gobind Singh, though readers differ on who wrote it. Either way, the two saloks sit side by side, like a conversation across a prison wall.
Why three names and not one?
A remembrance that kept only the leader would lose the people who stood next to him.
In the story, the Guru was not alone in the worst room of his life, and the day doesn't let anyone forget who was there with him.

how: On the remembrance of Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom, Sikhs gather for kirtan and Ardas, including at Gurdwara Sis Ganj in Delhi, and remember Bhai Mati Das, Bhai Sati Das and Bhai Dayala with him.

games.q: you're planning the remembrance of Guru Tegh Bahadur at your gurdwara. whose names are said that day?
o: the Guru, with Mati Das, Sati Das and Dayala.
games.why: the three companions are kept beside him. Sikh memory keeps the friends in the light too.

practice: Set out three small things in a row, three stones, three coins, three cups, and with each one say a name, aloud or inside: Mati Das, Sati Das, Dayala.
Then sit with all three in front of you, breathe slowly, and let them stand, too, for the people who have stood beside you in a hard room. If you pray, you can say Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Bhai Dayala. One of the three companions of Guru Tegh Bahadur, with Bhai Mati Das and Bhai Sati Das, who would not give up their faith. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: saathi, a companion, one who goes along with you.

carryVoice: Your line: three companions. Three names, always said beside his. Go gently.
